questions.q: What is an audit list rule built from?
options: Audit criteria selected by a consultant on the Create Audit List Rule page, which together form the rule
A single fixed criterion that never changes across companies
The employee's job title alone
A random number generator
questions.explain: A consultant selects one or more audit criteria on the Create Audit List Rule page; together those criteria form the audit list rule.

questions.q: What is the difference between a report-level and an employee-level audit trigger?
options: There is no difference; both terms mean the same thing
An employee-level trigger only applies to managers
A report-level trigger evaluates the current report alone; an employee-level trigger looks backward across an employee's history
A report-level trigger can never be automated
questions.explain: Report-level rules catch one-off issues on a single report; employee-level rules catch patterns, like repeated missing-receipt declarations, across multiple reports over time.

questions.q: Which audit action is typically used for a clear-cut violation that needs no human judgment call, such as a banned expense type?
options: Waive receipts
Request more information
Complete audit
Reject expense report
questions.explain: Reject expense report sends the item straight back to the employee without routing it to an auditor, appropriate for clear-cut cases.

questions.q: In the worked example, why did Dana Oyelaran's report get flagged by TWO separate audit rules?
options: Because her report had a hotel charge over the $400/night threshold AND multiple missing-receipt declarations on the same trip
Because she forgot to submit the report on time
Because her business unit had no audit rules configured
Because audit rules only ever fire once per employee per year
questions.explain: Her report simultaneously violated the high-value hotel rule and a missing-receipt-count rule, triggering both independently.

questions.q: How does audit rule processing relate to manager approval in the expense lifecycle?
options: Audit rules run after an expense report has already been paid
Audit rules are a separate, typically earlier step from manager approval, not a replacement for it
Audit rules and manager approval are the exact same step
Manager approval always happens before any audit rule can run
questions.explain: In the worked example, the audit clears before the report ever reaches the manager for the separate approval step covered in the next lesson.
